questions.question: Ravikirti was the court poet of which ruler?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakeshin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ravikirti was the court poet of **Pulakeshin II**, a prominent ruler of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
• He is best known for composing the **Aihole inscription**, which details the achievements of Pulakeshin II.
 
• The Aihole inscription, written in Sanskrit, is inscribed at the Meguti Jain temple in Aihole, Karnataka.
 
• Ravikirti's inscription describes Pulakeshin II's military conquests, including his victory over Harshavardhana and his expansion of the Chalukya empire.
 
• This inscription is considered an important historical source for understanding the Chalukya dynasty and its socio-political context.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pulakeshin II (610–642 CE):**

 
 
• Pulakeshin II was one of the greatest rulers of the Chalukya dynasty and ruled from Badami in present-day Karnataka.
 
• He successfully resisted the northward expansion of Harshavardhana, as documented in Ravikirti's Aihole inscription.
 
• Under his reign, the Chalukya empire expanded to include large parts of the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Aihole:**
 
 
• Aihole is an important historical site known as the "Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture."
 
• It was a major cultural and architectural center during the Chalukya period.
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Chalukyas were a prominent South Indian dynasty that ruled from the 6th to the 12th century CE.
 
• They are known for their contributions to art, architecture, and literature, as seen in their temple constructions and inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Court Poets:**
 
 
• Court poets like Ravikirti played a crucial role in documenting the achievements of their patrons.
 
• Such inscriptions often combined historical records with poetic flourishes, serving as both propaganda and cultural artifacts.

questions.question: During the reign of which of the following Pallavas, Hiuen Tsang visited the Pallava capital Kanchi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narasimhavarman I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Narasimhavarman I:

__
 
• Narasimhavarman I, also known as Mamalla Narasimhavarman, ruled from around 630 to 668 CE.
 
• He was the son and successor of Mahendravarman I.
 
• Narasimhavarman I was a powerful ruler who conducted successful military campaigns, including against the Chalukyas. 
 
• It was during his reign that Hiuen Tsang, the Chinese Buddhist monk and traveler, visited the Pallava capital of Kanchi.
 
• Hiuen Tsang's accounts provide valuable insights into the political, social, and cultural conditions of the time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahendravarman I:**

 
 
• Mahendravarman I was a prominent ruler of the Pallava dynasty who ruled from around 600 to 630 CE.
 
• He was known for his patronage of art, literature, and architecture.
 
• During his reign, the foundation of the rock-cut temples of Mamallapuram (also known as Mahabalipuram) was laid. 
 
 
 
• **Mahendravarman II:**
 
 
• Mahendravarman II, also known as Mahendravarman Pallava, ruled from around 668 to 672 CE.
 
• He was the son and successor of Narasimhavarman I.
 
• Mahendravarman II is known for his patronage of art and architecture, particularly the Shore Temple at Mamallapuram. 
 
 

 
• Narasimhavarman II:

 
 
• Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha Pallava, ruled from around 700 to 728 CE.
 
• He was a prominent ruler of the Pallava dynasty and is remembered for his military conquests and architectural achievements.

questions.question: Pulakeshin II was the famous ruler of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pulakeshin II was one of the most prominent rulers of the **Chalukya dynasty**, which ruled large parts of southern and central India.
 
• He reigned during the early 7th century CE (circa 610-642 CE) and is best known for his military conquests and administrative capabilities.
 
• Pulakeshin II successfully repelled the northward expansion of **Harsha**, the ruler of Kannauj, in a significant battle near the Narmada River.
 
• He expanded the Chalukya Empire significantly, establishing control over Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh regions.
 
• The **Aihole inscription**, composed by his court poet Ravikirti, provides detailed accounts of his conquests and achievements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chalukya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chalukyas were divided into three branches: the Early Chalukyas (Badami Chalukyas), the Western Chalukyas, and the Eastern Chalukyas.
 
• They made significant contributions to art, architecture, and administration, including iconic temples at Badami, Aihole, and Pattadakal.
 
 
 
• **Aihole Inscription:**
 
 
• It is a Sanskrit inscription in Kannada script that details Pulakeshin II's victories and his valor.
 
• The inscription also describes Pulakeshin II as a great patron of culture and a skilled administrator.
 
 
 
• **Harsha:**
 
 
• He was a powerful ruler of northern India during the 7th century, and his empire extended across much of the Gangetic plain.
 
• His defeat by Pulakeshin II marked the southern boundary of his empire.
 
 
 
• **Pattadakal Temples:**
 
 
• Pattadakal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, showcases the architectural brilliance of the Chalukyas under Pulakeshin II's reign.
 
• These temples represent a fusion of Dravidian and Nagara architectural styles.

questions.question: Banabhatta was the court poet of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harshvardhana**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Baṇabhaṭṭa was a 7th - century Sanskrit prose writer and poet of India.
 
• He was the Asthana Kavi (court poet) in the court of King Harsha Vardhana, who reigned c. 606 - 647 CE in north India.
 
• Bana's principal works include a biography of Harsha, the Harshacharita (Deeds of Harsha), and one of the world's earliest novels, Kadambari.
 
• Baṇa died before finishing the novel and it was completed by his son Bhuṣaṇabhaţţa.
 
• Both these works are noted texts of Sanskrit literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ashoka Asoka, 304 – 232 BCE, also known as Ashoka the Great, was an Indian emperor of the Maurya Empire, son of Bindusara, who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE. 
 
• Ashoka promoted the spread of Buddhism across ancient Asia.
 
• Kumaragupta I was an emperor of the Gupta Empire of Ancient India. A son of the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II and queen Dhruvadevi, he seems to have maintained control of his inherited territory, which extended from Gujarat in the west to the Bengal region in the east.
 
• Bindusara, also Amitraghāta or Amitrochates was the second Mauryan emperor of India. He was the son of the dynasty's founder Chandragupta and the father of its most famous ruler Ashoka.

questions.question: Mahabalipuram Monuments were built in ________ dynasty architecture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Pallavas.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

__
 
• This group of sanctuaries, founded by the Pallava kings, was carved out of rock along the Coromandel coast in the 7th and 8th centuries.
 
• It is known especially for its rathas (temples in the form of chariots), mandapas (cave sanctuaries).
 
• The city of Mahabalipuram was founded by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman I.
 
• It has 40 ancient monuments and Hindu temples, including one of the largest open-air rock reliefs in the world: the Descent of the Ganges or Arjuna's Penance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur was built during the reign of the Chola emperor Rajaraja and designed by the famous architect Sama Varma between 1003 and 1010 AD.
 
• Tiruvalisvaram Temple at Brahmadesam, Uttarakailash temple at Tiruvadi, Rajarajeshwar temple at Tanjore, Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram were built by Chola emperor Rajaraja II and the temple is dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
• Some famous temple and monuments built during the period of Chalukyas:
 
 
• Badami cave Temples, Karnataka.
 
• Virupaksha Temple at Pattadakal.
 
• Ravana Phadi Cave, Aihole.
 
• Sangameshvara Temple, Pattadakal.

questions.question: 'Banabhatta', well known for his literary works, flourished during the reign of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harshavardhana.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Banabhatta was an** Indian poet **and **Sanskrit prose writer **of the 7th century AD.
 
• He was the **Asthana Kavi **in the court of** King Harsha Vardhana,** who reigned from **606 AD to 647 AD** in north India first from** Sthanvishvara (Thanesar),** and later** Kannauj.**
 
• The** Harshacharita (Deeds of Harsha),** a** biography **of Harsha, and** Kadambari,** one of the **world's first novels,** are among Banabhatta's most important writings. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshavardhana **was a ruler of India who ruled throughout** northern India.**
 
• He was a member of the** Vardhana dynasty,** and the younger brother of** Rajyavardhana**, a **king of Thanesar**, present-day Haryana, and was the son of** Prabhakaravardhana **who defeated the** Alchon Huna invaders.**
 
• When Harsha attempted to expand his Empire into the southern peninsula of India, he was** defeated **by the south Indian Emperor** Pulakeshin II** of the **Chalukya dynasty **in the** Battle of Narmada.**

questions.question: Who was the first feudatory of Pallavas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijayalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vijayalaya** was the founder of the **Chola dynasty** in South India.
 
• He captured Thanjavur (Tanjore) and made it his capital around the mid-9th century.
 
• Vijayalaya initially served as a **feudatory of the Pallavas** before establishing his own independent kingdom.
 
• The Chola dynasty under Vijayalaya and his successors expanded and became one of the most powerful and culturally sophisticated empires in South India.
 
• The Chola rule saw significant advancements in **art, architecture, and maritime trade.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harshvardhan**__

 __
 
• **Harshvardhan** was an Indian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE.
 
• He was not related to the Pallavas but was the ruler of the **Vardhana dynasty**.
 
• His capital was **Kannauj**, and he is known for his support of Buddhism and extensive literary contributions.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra**__
 __
 
• **Rajendra Chola I** was a significant ruler of the Chola dynasty who succeeded **Rajaraja Chola I**.
 
• He is known for his extensive military conquests and for expanding the Chola Empire beyond South India.
 
• Rajendra Chola I established a new capital at **Gangaikonda Cholapuram**.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**__
 
 
• **Ashoka** was an Indian emperor of the **Maurya Dynasty** who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• He is known for his role in the spread of **Buddhism** across Asia.
 
• Ashoka's reign predated the Pallavas by several centuries.

questions.question: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built during the reign of the ________ king Narasimhavarman it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pallava**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was constructed during the reign of the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha.
 
• It is one of the earliest stone-built temples in South India, dating back to the 8th century.
 
• The temple complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognized for its historical and architectural significance.
 
• The Shore Temple is renowned for its Dravidian architectural style and intricate carvings depicting various Hindu deities and mythological scenes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pallava Dynasty**

 
 
• The Pallava dynasty ruled parts of South India from the 3rd century to the 9th century AD.
 
• Their capital was Kanchipuram, a significant cultural and religious center.
 
• The Pallavas were known for their patronage of arts, architecture, and education.
 
• They played a crucial role in the development of Dravidian architecture, as seen in their rock-cut temples and sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Mahabalipuram**
 
 
• Mahabalipuram, also known as Mamallapuram, is a historic town in Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is famous for its rock-cut caves, monolithic structures, and temples built during the Pallava period.
 
• The site includes landmarks like the Pancha Rathas, Arjuna's Penance, and the Shore Temple.
 
• Mahabalipuram is a popular tourist destination and a significant archaeological site.
 
 
 
• **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha)**
 
 
• Narasimhavarman II, also known as Rajasimha, was a prominent Pallava ruler who reigned during the 7th and 8th centuries.
 
• He is credited with the construction of several architectural marvels in Mahabalipuram, including the Shore Temple.
 
• Under his rule, the Pallava kingdom experienced a period of cultural and artistic flourishing.
 
• Rajasimha's contributions to temple architecture have left a lasting legacy in South Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Architecture**
 
 
• Dravidian architecture is a style of temple architecture that emerged in Southern India.
 
• It is characterized by pyramid-shaped towers (vimanas), intricate sculptures, and elaborate carvings.
 
• Prominent examples include the Brihadeeswarar Temple, Meenakshi Temple, and Shore Temple.
 
• This architectural style significantly influenced the construction of Hindu temples across South India and Southeast Asia.

questions.question: The sister of Harshavardhana Rajyashri was married to__________, the king of Maukhari dynasty of Kanyakubja.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Grahavarman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rajyashri, the sister of Harshavardhana, was married to Grahavarman.
 
• Grahavarman was the king of the Maukhari dynasty, which ruled over Kanyakubja (modern-day Kannauj).
 
• The Maukhari dynasty played a significant role in the political landscape of northern India during the early medieval period.
 
• The marriage alliance between Rajyashri and Grahavarman helped strengthen the political ties between the Vardhana dynasty and the Maukhari dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshavardhana**

 
 
• Harshavardhana, also known as Harsha, was a prominent Indian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE.
 
• He belonged to the Vardhana dynasty and was known for his efforts to establish a strong and unified empire in northern India.
 
• Harsha was a patron of arts and culture, and his court was adorned with scholars like Banabhatta and Xuanzang.
 
• His reign marked a period of prosperity and cultural flourishing in North India.
 
 
 
• **Maukhari Dynasty**
 
 
• The Maukhari dynasty was an influential ruling dynasty in North India during the 6th and 7th centuries CE.
 
• They initially served as vassals of the Gupta Empire before establishing their independent rule.
 
• The Maukhari rulers were known for their administrative efficiency and military prowess.
 
• Their capital was Kanyakubja (Kannauj), which became a significant center of power in North India.
 
 
 
• **Kanyakubja (Kannauj)**
 
 
• Kanyakubja, also known as Kannauj, is an ancient city located in the present-day Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It has been a prominent political, cultural, and commercial center since ancient times.
 
• Kannauj was known for its rich cultural heritage and was a major center of learning and arts.
 
• Throughout history, Kannauj has been a coveted seat of power for various dynasties, including the Maukhari and the Vardhana dynasties.
 
 
 
• **Political Alliances in Ancient India**
 
 
• Marriage alliances were a common strategy for establishing political ties and securing peace between different dynasties.
 
• Such alliances helped in strengthening mutual trust and cooperation between ruling families.
 
• They played a crucial role in the consolidation of power and expansion of empires in ancient India.
 
• These alliances also facilitated cultural exchange and integration between different regions.

questions.question: Harshvardhan's ambitions of extending his power to Deccan and South India were stopped by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pulakesin II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pulakesin II was a renowned Chalukya king who ruled over the Deccan region.
 
• Harshavardhana, the ruler of North India, attempted to expand his influence to the Deccan and South India.
 
• Pulakesin II decisively defeated Harshavardhana near the banks of the river Narmada around 618-619 AD, halting his southern expansion.
 
• This victory is recorded in the Aihole inscription, composed by Pulakesin II's court poet, Ravikirti.
 
• The defeat of Harshavardhana by Pulakesin II is considered a significant event in Indian history as it marked the limit of Harshavardhana's territorial expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshavardhana**

 
 
• Harshavardhana, also known as Harsha, was an Indian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 AD.
 
• He established his capital at Kannauj and was known for his patronage of arts and literature.
 
• Harsha's reign is well-documented by the Chinese traveler Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang).
 
 
 
• **Chalukya Dynasty**
 
 
• The Chalukya dynasty was an important South Indian dynasty that ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and 12th centuries.
 
• Pulakesin II was one of the most notable rulers of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Aihole Inscription**
 
 
• The Aihole inscription is a famous historical record composed by Ravikirti, the court poet of Pulakesin II.
 
• It documents the achievements of Pulakesin II, including his victory over Harshavardhana.
 
 
 
• **Narmada River**
 
 
• The Narmada River is one of the major rivers in central India, flowing westwards over a length of about 1,312 km.
 
• The battle between Harshavardhana and Pulakesin II took place near this river.
